question: The dimensions of the basketball court is measured ______ from the inner edge of the boundary line.
solution:
The correct answer is__** 28 × 15 m.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **basketball court** is a **rectangular court** with a standard size of **28 meters** in length and **15 meters** in width.
 
• The measurements are taken from the **inner edge **of the boundary line, which marks the playing area of the court.
 
• The playing area, with **baskets at either end**, is the basketball court. 
 
• The rims of each basket on an indoor basketball court are typically **3.048 meters high** and are almost always made of **polished wood**, typically maple.
 
• Common paving materials like **concrete or asphalt **are used to create outdoor surfaces.
 
• **Glass basketball courts** may be used in international competitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The main goal of **basketball**, a team sport, is to **shoot a basketball **through the opponent's hoop while keeping the other team from doing the same.
 
• **Two teams,** usually consisting of **five players** each, engage in this activity. 
 
• Unless it is made from behind the three-point line, in which case it is for three points, a** field goal** is worth** two.** 
 
• Following a foul, the player who was fouled or chosen to shoot a technical foul is awarded **one, two, or three one-point free throws**.
 
• The timed play then **ends. **
 
• The team with the** most points** at the end of regulation play wins; however, if the score is tied at the completion of regulation play,** overtime** must be played.
